newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ABN AMRO Bank sees growth in Brazil market.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO Bank sees growth in Brazil market.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO Holding NV said it expects over the next few years to expand its corporate, investment and consumer banking activities in Brazil, the third most important country for the bank in terms of profits after the Netherlands and the U.S.

"We think we are well placed to grow further and increase our market share in all these segments: corporate, commercial, consumer finance and investment banking," Jan Kalff, ABN AMRO Bank's Managing Board Chairman, told a news conference here, without projecting figures.

Kalff, who is on a five-day trip to Brazil, Chile and Argentina, said ABN AMRO Bank, which has 50 branches in the country, might open a few more branches to expand its consumer finance operations, but noted "the growth will come from our presence and branch network."
ABN AMRO Bank is a leading institution in consumer finance in Brazil, mainly in the car loans business. Its total loan portfolio currently amounts to $1.250 billion, nearly double last year's.

"We are very optimistic about the growth potential of credit finance operations. This market has just begun to grow," said Fabio Barbosa, ABN AMRO Bank president in Brazil, adding he expects the country's consumer credit market to double over the next five years.
Project finance is another segment in which ABN AMRO Bank is particularly interested in increasing its participation.
"The upcoming privatizations of the telecommunications and power sectors will represent good opportunities for us as they will require long-term financing," said Barbosa.

Currently ABN AMRO Bank is an advisor for U.S. telecom firm GTE Corp on the bidding process for Brazil's Band B cellular services and the sale of a 35 percent stake in Rio Grande do Sul state's telecom firm Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT).

It is also working as an advisor for U.S. companies on Brazilian power privatizations. The bank is also eyeing Sao Paulo state's power privatizations and has been holding talks with local consulting firm Projeta and the UK's Rothschild, a partner of ABN AMRO Bank in the international equity business, to bid to become advisors on the selloffs.
ABN AMRO's plans for Brazil do not involve acquisitions of other banks, ABN AMRO's chairman said.
"We don't really need to acquire another bank because we have internal growth. We can never say never but I do not expect it," he said.

ABN AMRO Bank has 124 branches in 12 countries in Latin America and Caribbean, with $5.4 billion in total assets, according to 1995 figures. In Brazil, where the bank has been present since 1917, ABN AMRO Bank ranks the sixth position among around 40 foreign banks, with a net worth estimated at $165 million, it added.
